segments: ...filled it and killed those whom they found in it.
For the multitude of the people had fled to a small island nearby;
and when these [people] were hoping {OCR?} [for mercy] from the Egyptian Arabs,
Frankish raiders came upon them and plundered all their possessions,
even to the point that they stripped them of their clothes;
however, they did not kill them.
Then the Egyptians quickly arrived from Ayas at Mopsuestia on Tuesday,
and they made a great slaughter in it,
and burned it completely.
And they crossed the bridge,
and spread throughout the whole country.
Some of them went toward Tarsus,
and on Saturday, the feast of the Arabs, they called to prayer from its tower,
and they spread as far as Corycus,
killing, taking captive, and burning.
Others of them turned toward Sis,
and they found no one in it,
for all of them were fortified in its citadel;
and they burned it partially.
And there were killed twenty-five
monks in the monastery of Paximates, along with Rabban Solomon, the venerable elder
and syncellus of the late Patriarch Mor Ignatius.
And they burned that monastery,
and also the monastery of Gwikath and the rest of the dwellings and monasteries of the Armenians and Greeks.
And as for the little monastery of our Patriarch,
which was in the district of Sis,
they left it as if it had never existed.
The Patriarch, however, fled to the fortress of Bahga,
and hid there until the wrath had passed.
The Egyptians remained in the country until Low Sunday was past,
and they departed, carrying off immense plunder.
The number of the slain amounted to sixty thousand,
and for the women and children who were led into captivity, there was no number.
Now there were in that country about ten thousand Turkmens,
and they also caused destruction among the Christians.
And when the Egyptians departed,
the King killed all of them,
and enslaved their families,
and plundered all their possessions.
And in that same year died Bohemond, Prince of Tripoli,
and his son reigned in his place.
And the nobles sent and brought Lord {OCR?} ... of Paximates
